facts.text: I had my left knee replaced and went home from hospital about 15 days ago.
When I went home after the knee operation I was put on enoxaparin injections, 40 mg under the skin once a day, to prevent blood clots.
No blood tests to check my platelets were planned after I went home.
My right side suddenly became weak.
I had one episode, lasting about 2 minutes, when I wasn't fully conscious.

facts.item: shaking of the right leg and belly
facts.text: During that episode my right leg and my belly were shaking.

facts.item: pain in the upper right abdomen
facts.text: I have pain in the upper right part of my belly.
I don't have high blood pressure.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Right upper quadrant pain, without hepatosplenomegaly.

findings.name: brain MRI
findings.result: Acute infarct in the left precentral and postcentral gyri; subacute infarct in the right parietal lobe.

findings.name: echocardiography
findings.result: Nondilated left atrium; normal ejection fraction (65%); no intracardiac thrombus.

findings.name: CT pulmonary angiography
findings.result: Pulmonary emboli in the left main and segmental arteries.

findings.name: abdominal CT
findings.result: Filling defects in branches of the right suprahepatic vein.

findings.name: venous ultrasound of the left leg
findings.result: Nonacute thrombosis of the superficial femoral and popliteal veins.

findings.name: repeat platelet count in citrated blood
findings.time: repeat count after the initial result

gold.reasoning: 1. Carotid atherosclerotic disease was ruled out because “the ultrasound of the supra-aortic trunks was also normal.” 2. Pseudothrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, and autoimmune thrombocytopenia were excluded, as supported by “the clinical suspicion of a HIT diagnosis was supported by… the exclusion of a thrombocytopenia due to splenomegaly, pseudothrombocytopenia, and autoimmune thrombocytopenia.”

f001: 'Fifteen days later' may count from the operation or from discharge; the text keeps both events together without fixing which.
f002: The source says she was discharged on enoxaparin; that she was still taking it 15 days later is assumed (time current).
f007: A patient may not remember an episode of altered consciousness herself; written as what she knows about the episode.
f009: Taken from the physical examination (s007); pain is something the patient feels.

x007: Unit corrected from the source's 'ηg/L' (typo) to ng/L.
x008: The source says only 'other values were within normal limits' without naming the tests; kept as one generic record.
x010: The source's 'excluding atrial fibrillation' is the clinician's inference from ECG and echo together; the echo result keeps the report findings (no intracardiac thrombus) and the rhythm is in the ECG record.

leakage.reason: Only the alias 'low-molecular-weight heparin' contains 'heparin'; it names the drug class the patient takes, so the controller can match questions about heparin.
The repeat citrate platelet count reports 'thrombocytopenia', part of the gold name; this is the test's answer.

source_issues: Platelet count '43 000 × 10^9/L' mixes units (43 × 10^9/L or 43 000/µL intended); kept as written.
D-dimer unit written 'ηg/L' (Greek eta), an obvious typo for ng/L.
Focal tremors 'in her right leg and abdomen' is unusual wording; kept.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation 15 days after left knee replacement with fever, headache, acute right-sided weakness and a 2-minute episode of altered consciousness (s002); the imaging, laboratory tests and ultrasounds (s003-s012) are the workup of this presentation.
The knee replacement and enoxaparin prophylaxis (s001) are history before the index visit.
Mucocutaneous bleeding and hepatosplenomegaly are examination negatives and stay in the findings only.
